_provenance.source: Hand-authored for the MNO-B corpus (multi-mno-nora strand). See docs/compact/strands/multi-mno-nora/mno-b-spec.md + D-DRAFT-1..4.
_provenance.model: leading_id_body — a single PDF whose top-level chapters are plans; requirements are flat body paragraphs that begin with <PREFIX>-<PLAN>-<DIGITS>; sections/subsections are non-requirement context.
_provenance.disabled_detections: revision-history (signal + label), glossary/definitions, and reference-list detection are OFF — this corpus has none of those sections, and the signal-based revhist path false-positived a content table as a changelog.
_provenance.placeholders: Proprietary tokens are placeholders per D-062. The literal req_id common prefix is <MNO0> — map it to the real value in customizations/mappings/bs_5114ac92.json (work-PC mapping; pushed to company-internal git only). Structural values (numbering, font sizes, content_start) are literal and corpus-safe.
_provenance.id_pattern_precision: requirement_id.pattern deliberately uses a BOUNDED, space-free plan-token class instead of the generic <PLAN> placeholder. Under this profile's leading_text anchor the id regex is start-anchored with no end bound, so a token class containing a bare space (as generic <PLAN> does) runs greedily across prose and swallows requirement text into the id; whitespace normalization then welds it into one token, silently corrupting ids. Field-validated: the real plan-token inventory contains no spaces and no hyphens, so whitespace tolerance is needed ONLY to heal an id broken beside a separator and is expressed as a scoped \s? adjacent to each separator. Do NOT reintroduce a bare space or an unbounded run into this class. The length bound carries headroom over the observed inventory; a token exceeding it fails to match and surfaces as a no-id skip in the adapter (visible loss) rather than a corrupted id (silent corruption) — the deliberate trade. Same class is safe under end-bounded anchors (anchor=last_run), so the hazard is class x anchor, not the class alone.
